baseline_provenance.note: Live main is read by object; the checkout is not moved. The hook routes merge-base(origin/main)..head for a new branch, so fetch origin main before the first push and re-measure the route then.

resource_identities.net:netns-4026531840|tcp|0.0.0.0|443: Destination identity, measured not inferred. The remote is read from the vehicle itself: `git remote -v` gives origin = https://github.com/CaptTymur/skipi-crewing.git for both fetch and push, i.e. HTTPS, hence port 443 and not the 22 the ledger's existing GitHub entry uses. The namespace is MY measurement: `readlink /proc/self/ns/net` = net:[4026531840], the same inode the ledger spells netns-4026531840, so this stage shares that namespace rather than sitting in one of its own. The address slot is 0.0.0.0 - the schema's 'honest broadest' - and that choice is deliberate: github.com resolved to 140.82.121.3 at 15:43Z by `getent ahostsv4` (the very address the ledger's SSH entry pins), but GitHub rotates its addresses and a pinned IP that the fetch does not actually reach would be a declaration that is false precisely when it matters, hiding a collision instead of raising one. 0.0.0.0 overlaps any address on tcp/443 in this namespace, which is the conservative direction. It correctly does NOT collide with the existing tcp/22 GitHub entry: a different port is a different resource. The DNS lookup itself was a local resolver query made while building this request; it changes no remote state and is not the stage's action.

streams.what_this_stage_does_NOT_do: It does not run skipi-guard and produces no route VERDICT. It records the route INPUT - merge-base and the triple-dot file list - because after a fetch those are already facts on disk and writing them down costs nothing; a verdict needs the guard, and the coordinator placed that in its own request. It does not push, does not create a PR, does not touch src-tauri/Cargo.{toml,lock}, and does not create or push any v* tag.
streams.why_the_stage_token_is_INTEGRATE: Stage 4 declared IMPLEMENT because a commit makes the artefact. The tail integrates it, so INTEGRATE is the honest token. Checked rather than assumed that this is legal: the gate's 'invalid stage transition' at stage_gate.py:242 governs the lease ACTION (start/stop/complete/ack-stop), not the ordering of stage NAMES, and INTEGRATE is in the schema's allowed set. The driver's ACK_START document carried a hard-coded "stage":"IMPLEMENT" from being copied off the stage-4 driver; it now says INTEGRATE, which is the sixth inherited-text defect of this class in a copied driver and the reason check-driver-prose.py exists.
streams.the_cache_is_ALREADY_fresh_and_this_fetc: Measured at 15:49Z by `ls-remote origin refs/heads/main`: live main = f145c6017eaea3804a5429e5aa428b6fb0ece6d9, cached origin/main = the same value, and that is also my commit's parent. streams.the_route_input_is_provably_stable_under: A worry worth closing with a measurement rather than a hope: if main advances between now and the push, does my routed set grow and cost me the route? No. `merge-base --is-ancestor f145c601 <live main>` is TRUE, and my HEAD is a single commit whose parent is f145c601, so merge-base(X, e5132934) = f145c601 for ANY X descending from f145c601 - the triple-dot range stays my four files and the route stays crewing-635-single-user. The one case that breaks it is main being force-pushed onto something that is not a descendant of f145c601, which would move the merge-base and would be visible in the measurement. This is the mirror image of the failure in my notes: there a STALE origin/main sat as an ANCESTOR of the work's base and silently widened the range to 6-8 files, losing the route. Here the cached ref IS the base, so the range is already minimal.
streams.a_predicate_defect_I_found_in_my_own_reh: The insurance the coordinator asked for was 'count the refs before and after and treat any change you did not cause as a finding'. My first implementation counted `find "$GITDIR/refs/remotes" -type f | wc -l`. Rehearsed against a local bare remote it printed `FINDING: refs/remotes went 1 -> 2` on a fetch that added nothing: `find -type f` sees LOOSE files only, so a ref moving from the packed-refs file to a loose file reads as a new ref. A predicate that cries wolf on re-packing is worse than none, because the finding it exists to report would be indistinguishable from its own noise. Replaced with a NAME SET from `for-each-ref`, comparing membership and reporting ADDED and GONE by name: it does not care whether a ref is packed, and it names the ref instead of implying one. In the real repo both methods happen to agree at 149 (nothing is packed there today) - which is exactly why the fixture, not the repo, is what exposed it.
streams.my_first_drill_of_the_replacement_was_a_: Having replaced the predicate I drilled it by rewriting the driver's fetch line to a bare `git fetch origin` with a second branch waiting on the fixture remote, so a ref would arrive during the fetch. It reported nothing, and 'no finding' was the answer I wanted. The reason was not the predicate: my sed pattern was `git fetch origin main` while the real line reads `git -C "$WT" fetch origin main`, so the substitution matched nothing and I had re-run the UNMODIFIED script against itself. `diff` of the two drivers was empty - the control that caught it - and a manual bare fetch proved the fixture would indeed have shown the ref. Re-drilled with the correct pattern the predicate fires and names it: `FINDING: remote ref NAMES changed - added [refs/remotes/origin/other] gone []`, while the real explicit refspec on the same fixture stays silent. Both halves measured, which is the only form in which a 'silent' instrument means anything. This is the same genus as the needles in my notes: the drill must be a legal mutation whose whole output I read, and an unmutated subject answers a different question.
streams.why_evidence_files_holds_the_driver_alon: Earlier stages pinned the four product files. For a fetch that would be weaker, not stronger: the gate's own live snapshot already re-reads `repo`, `head` and `status_sha256` for the declared repo, and a porcelain-EMPTY worktree in the -uall unit is a statement about EVERY file in the tree, whereas four digests are a statement about four. The driver checks the same emptiness before and after. So the tree is pinned by the gate plus the ref value, and evidence_files carries the one object this review actually rests on - the executable. Its sha256 is also printed by the driver at run time and recorded into both ACK documents.
streams.a_finding_about_the_coordinator_s_OWN_ne: While choosing the token form I measured `overlaps()` (inspect_requests.py:47-54) and found a blind spot worth naming, since I am the first writer in this task to declare a `net:` surface. The namespace field is compared by STRING EQUALITY, and only the ADDRESS field gets `is_unspecified` treatment. The ledger already carries one physical namespace under four spellings - `netns-4026531840` (93 tokens), `4026531840` (48+), `[4026531840]` and `net:[4026531840]`. Measured: `netns-4026531840|tcp|0.0.0.0|443` vs `4026531840|tcp|140.82.121.4|443` -> False. Two writers in the SAME netns, one of them honestly declaring the broadest address, do not collide if they spell the namespace differently - so the broad declaration buys nothing against them. I therefore spell it `netns-4026531840`, matching the dominant form, so that my declaration CAN collide with the existing GitHub entry. Naming it here rather than proposing a verifier change: the schema says this verifier is not edited amid live streams, and the same reasoning applies.
streams.resource_identities_note: One net resource, declared above. No database, no port binding (this stage LISTENS on nothing - the token is outbound egress and sits in `ports.reads`, because a fetch reads from the remote and changes nothing there; the later push is the write). GIT BYTES yes, and they are the subject: declared by exact path - FETCH_HEAD and refs/remotes/origin/main inside the shared gitdir - rather than as the whole .git, because the gitdir is shared with 85 linked worktrees and claiming all of it would collide with every neighbour over bytes I do not touch.
